clocks.label: UAE ENVOY 48H
clocks.why: Algiers gave the Emirati ambassador two days to comply with the severance. This clock prices GEO-030, opened today at 40 per cent: whether the rupture acquires an INSTRUMENT. Expiry with an ambassador on a plane and nothing else is a gesture; expiry alongside a named concession is a proxy war going commercial.

clocks.label: FOMC DECISION
clocks.why: The meeting behind GEO-029 at 65 per cent, raised two points today because the ECB abandoned look-through first. Three members already dissented FOR a hike in July, PCE runs 3.7 per cent, and Brent is now $105-107. This decides whether the world's reserve central bank tightens INTO an oil supply shock - and remember the horizon holds three meetings, not one.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: Two days after the Fed, and the clock behind GEO-025 at 29 per cent, held today as a LIMITATION rather than a judgement because no fresh live yen spot was established. The carry unwind needs both legs; a Tokyo hike into a hawkish Fed is the August 2024 template exactly.

clocks.label: BAB EL-MANDEB COUNT
clocks.why: The weekly transit count against Lloyd's List Intelligence's published pre-Mocha baseline of 273 a week - the falsifier on today's lead card. Thursday printed 12 in a day against 30. This is the number that decides whether a map change was a world event or a headline.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Our own dated falsifier, published in advance so it can be scored against us, with two legs: an attack on a laden tanker inside the international lanes, and Iran publishing coordinates for its restricted zone or an Omani co-signature. Neither has landed. Non-occurrence scores against the escalation model - it does not get quietly rolled forward.

clocks.label: XI STATE VISIT
clocks.why: The visit GEO-006 rides at 90 per cent and GEO-012 at 31, now carrying a numbered deliverable of reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each way, which is what turned GEO-007 down to 18. It also carries the tell for the Hidden-Strategy Watch: whether Chinese coast guard presence east of Taiwan persists THROUGH the visit.

speculation.obs: Specialist imagery and OSINT accounts have been documenting airstrips on the two islands in and beside the strait since well before anyone was fighting for them. As reported by The War Zone, Planet Labs satellite imagery from 2025 documented runways on both Perim (Mayyun) and Zuqar - Perim's roughly 6,150 feet long and built by the UAE, Zuqar's constructed in 2025 alongside government shipping-tracking installations - and the accounts OSINTtechnical, Osint613, Open Source Intel and AfriMEOSINT separately documented Houthi forces at Mokha airport and captured equipment this week.
speculation.src: Planet Labs imagery and named OSINT accounts, compiled by The War Zone
speculation.read: Labelled inference. A 6,150-foot runway on a two-square-mile volcanic rock is not an airfield for local traffic - it is a platform, and the UAE built it during its own Yemen intervention for exactly the reason it is valuable now. The inference is that whoever takes Perim inherits not just a position in the shipping lane but a hardened piece of infrastructure capable of basing aircraft over the strait, which changes the cost of retaking it by an order of magnitude. Note what this reframes: the argument over whether Ansar Allah 'holds' Perim is usually conducted as a question about ground troops, when the observable that would actually matter is aircraft or radar on that runway.
speculation.falsifier: Imagery showing aircraft, air-defence or radar emplaced on the Perim or Zuqar strips confirms the platform reading and means the islands are being used rather than merely occupied. Imagery showing the strips cratered, or continued absence of any airframe on them through end-September, kills it and says the runways are a legacy artefact rather than a live capability.

speculation.obs: The hull counters are showing the OTHER chokepoint thinning while everyone watches this one. As reported by The War Zone citing Reuters preliminary data, vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz fell on Wednesday to seven from twelve the previous day, against a ten-day average of fourteen - and separately Lloyd's List Intelligence recorded 273 ships a week through Bab el-Mandeb between 27 July and 23 August, a roughly 15 per cent reduction rather than a stoppage.
speculation.src: Lloyd's List Intelligence and Reuters preliminary transit data, via The War Zone
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and the inference is about attention rather than about ships. Fourteen transits a day through Hormuz is a fraction of a normal book, and seven is half of that already-diminished number - which means the strait that dominated this board for months has quietly become a trickle while the coverage moved to Bab el-Mandeb. If both doors are constricted at once, the Cape reroute is not an alternative for Gulf distillate, it is the only route, and that is the physical fact underneath tonight's record diesel crack. The caution: single-day transit counts are noisy, preliminary and revised, and one Wednesday is not a trend.
speculation.falsifier: A Hormuz weekly average holding below ten transits a day through end-September confirms that the Gulf's own door is the binding constraint and that the diesel crack has a floor under it. A recovery toward the twenty-plus range, or a revision of these preliminary counts upward, kills the reading and puts the distillate story back on Bab el-Mandeb alone.

speculation.obs: Imagery analysts are watching a Chinese base nobody is reporting on build out at speed. As documented in satellite imagery captured between 2 July and 1 September 2026 and analysed by Misbar, construction at China's Lop Nur air base accelerated markedly over that window - a major concrete taxiway running parallel to the runway and connecting to central buildings was near complete by early September, alongside a circular apron roughly 130 metres in diameter at the northern end of the base.
speculation.read: Labelled inference. Lop Nur is the site of China's nuclear test programme, so any construction there is read against a testing question rather than a basing one - but a parallel taxiway and a large circular apron are airfield throughput features, which is the signature of a base being prepared to cycle aircraft rather than to host an event. The honest read is that this is infrastructure with several possible purposes and no announced one, which is precisely the species worth logging: a physical thing observed, at a politically loaded location, with no official story attached. Do not let the location supply the conclusion.
speculation.falsifier: Aircraft or support equipment appearing on the new apron in subsequent passes confirms the throughput reading. Seismic activity at the Lop Nur test site, or construction visibly serving the test infrastructure rather than the runway, points at the other explanation entirely and kills the airfield reading.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

The war has reached the LOADING POINT: Iranian state media says four US missiles hit a tanker six miles off Kharg on 5 September, and Iran fired anti-ship and ballistic missiles toward the strait the day before. Unconfirmed, and the terminals themselves are still unstruck - but the one asset with any convertible value left is now inside the target set

A SECOND CHOKEPOINT, bought without an Iranian casualty: with Ansar Allah holding the Yemeni bank of Bab el-Mandeb, Tehran now has a hand on two of the six places where seaborne trade passes single file. Note what that does to the bargaining table rather than the battlefield - a Red Sea chip is SEPARABLE, tradeable away without Iran conceding anything of its own, which makes a Hormuz settlement cheaper for Tehran and not more expensive. The principal-agent risk runs the other way: Ansar Allah has its own war aims at Taiz and its own scores with Riyadh, and a proxy that acquires territory acquires independence

dossiers.name: Saudi Arabia

glance.government: Absolute monarchy; day-to-day rule exercised by Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman on behalf of King Salman
glance.leader: Mohammed bin Salman, Crown Prince and PM; the decisive desks are the Royal Court, the Ministry of Defence under Khalid bin Salman, and Aramco
glance.gdp: Roughly $1.1tn nominal; fiscal breakeven oil price is materially above the pre-war Brent strip, which is why a high barrel is not simply good news for Riyadh
glance.military: About 250,000 active across services plus the SANG; heavily equipped and air-dominant, with a demonstrated shortage of deployable INFANTRY - the constraint that just cost it Mocha
glance.influence: Spare crude capacity, Ras Tanura and Yanbu as the world's principal loading complex, and since the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement a publicly stated Pakistani security commitment

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint. Riyadh's problem is not resolve, it is force structure: it can generate fifty-four air strikes in a day and cannot generate a brigade that will hold a coastline, which is why its Yemeni position is a patchwork of rival Saudi- and Emirati-funded militias that has now lost the last Red Sea port it held south of Hodeidah. The desk that decides is the Royal Court plus Aramco, not the foreign ministry - and Aramco's interest is a barrel high enough to fund Vision 2030 and low enough not to invite demand destruction or an American price intervention, which is a narrow band the war keeps pushing it out of. The kingdom is now absorbing ballistic missiles and drones at Khamis Mushait, Abha and Jazan while its refining capacity is repeatedly knocked over, and the historical base rate says it will absorb them: Abqaiq in 2019 removed half of Saudi output and produced no American strike on Iran. What is new is that Islamabad has publicly said the Mecca pact 'will definitely make this agreement operational' if aggression spills further into the kingdom - a nuclear-armed state attaching itself to one side of a proxy war. The falsifier is a strike on an EXPORT terminal rather than a refinery: that is the rung at which Riyadh stops taxing its own margins and starts losing its only convertible asset, and it is where American calculus historically changes.

concerns: No deployable ground force in Yemen - the coalition's Giants Brigades, Nation's Shield, National Resistance and Taizi units withdrew from Mocha rather than hold it, and air power cannot retake a coast
Refining capacity is being taxed repeatedly: Jazan, 400,000 b/d and about a tenth of Aramco's net refining, has been hit or shut three times since late July
Export infrastructure at Ras Tanura and Yanbu remains untouched - the single most consequential unfired tripwire on this board

The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement now has a public Pakistani statement of operational intent attached to it, which converts a deterrent into a commitment with an escalation ladder Riyadh does not fully control
Fiscal breakeven above the strip means a war premium does not simply pay for itself; the kingdom needs volume as much as price, and volume is what a terminal strike would take

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

First reciprocated pause of the war, and it is a bargaining instrument rather than fatigue: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight on 5 September, explicitly tied to the American envoys' visit, hours after striking Ukrainian airports and infrastructure and with Ryabkov restating that Washington must accept realities on the ground

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; sixteen Laender, each electing its own Minister-President. Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote 20 September 2026
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor, whose CDU just lost 25 of its 40 seats in Saxony-Anhalt; Ulrich Siegmund leads the AfD there and has said he will not stand for Minister-President without a stable majority
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; Jaguar Land Rover cutting 4,000 jobs and Volkswagen repurposing a plant for defence are the texture of the industrial quarter
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with rearmament running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint stopped being abstract on Sunday. The AfD took 43.9 per cent and 39 of 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt on turnout that rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent, and the CDU fell to 17.2 per cent - which means the late-mobilisation argument that has contained the AfD in every previous Land election did not work, and ING said so in as many words. The desk that now decides is not the federal party presidium in Berlin, which can only expel people; it is the Landtag running ballots in Magdeburg, where a third round for Minister-President is settled by a simple majority of votes cast and the five-seat BSW can decide the outcome by abstaining. Underneath the politics the older vice is unchanged: Germany replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, trading a political dependency for a maritime one, so a war at Hormuz reaches German industry directly - and it remains the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is why a drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Two more elections land on 20 September.

concerns: A Land where no majority exists without breaking one of two taboos - the CDU has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke, and the third-ballot rule rewards deadlock
Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote on 20 September, thirteen days after the mobilisation defence visibly failed
Fraud narratives spread within hours of the count, part of them traced by DW's fact-check desk to the Matryoshka influence operation - contested results are now a standing feature of German elections
A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold, and Lavrov has answered Berlin's attribution by calling it the start of a real war
Energy input cost remains the binding industrial number, and seaborne LNG means Hormuz is now a German domestic-politics variable

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the offices that matter for this file are the Bank of Japan policy board and the Ministry of Finance FX desk - not the cabinet
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan's constraint became visible in a number this week: 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, spent in a single month defending the currency, and reporting that it likely sold US Treasuries to fund it. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology; that arrangement is unwinding because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption made worse. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September, and the yen has already run to 154.06 on the expectation. What is genuinely new is the American side of the plumbing: Washington joined the July intervention and Bessent pushed the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility, which lets Tokyo borrow dollars against its Treasuries instead of selling them. Read that as the balance-of-financial-terror being actively managed - the US needs its largest foreign creditor not to become a seller during a heavy issuance calendar, and it built a valve to make sure.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
A currency defence funded by Treasury sales raises US long-end yields at the exact moment the ten-year sits above 4.75 per cent
A defence financed by repo must be repeatedly refinanced, which converts a one-off intervention into a standing obligation
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if Bab el-Mandeb closes in practice rather than in rhetoric?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is an underwriting decision, not a naval one. The strait has stayed open on a BELIEF - that the Houthi threat is addressed to Saudi-linked tonnage rather than the general trade - and a belief reprices in an afternoon in a way a minefield does not. Holding the bank changes the physics: shore-launched anti-ship missiles and even tube artillery from covered positions cannot be intercepted away, and retaking the coast requires infantry the Saudi-backed coalition has just shown it does not have. The first casualty is not oil, which mostly leaves the Gulf eastward, but DIESEL heading to Europe and containers heading to the Mediterranean - and behind them Egypt, whose Suez receipts are a top-three hard-currency earner under an IMF programme.

stages.s: A - transits recover toward the 273-a-week baseline within a fortnight as owners test the threat and find it still addressed to Saudi hulls; Mocha bought position, not closure
B - transits settle at a materially lower plateau with war-risk premia repricing above one per cent of hull value; a partial, priced closure that persists
C - war-risk quotes stop distinguishing tonnage classes and mainline carriers formally reroute via the Cape; Suez volumes and Egyptian receipts fall sharply
D - a multinational naval escort or ground operation is announced to retake the coast

scenarios.falsifier: Weekly Bab el-Mandeb transits holding near 270 through 30 September with war-risk still quoted differentially by tonnage class. If they hold, stage A is the correct model and stages C and D should be cut hard - and this desk will have over-weighted a map change.

scenarios.q: What if the Fed hikes on 16 September into a $107 barrel?
scenarios.read: A hike does not produce a barrel, and every participant knows it - so the decision is about credibility rather than about supply, which is what makes it consequential. The ECB moved first this morning and said out loud that it is preparing for longer-lasting inflation, which raises the cost to a new Fed chair of being the one who blinked. Watch the CURVE rather than the headline: a hike that flattens the curve says the market believes the Fed will crush demand and take the recession; a hike that steepens it says the market thinks tightening into a supply shock is an error it will have to be paid to hold. The second leg matters too - the BoJ meets two days later, and a hawkish Fed plus a hawkish BoJ is the exact configuration that unwound the yen carry trade in August 2024.

stages.s: A - a 25bp hike with the curve flattening; the market accepts the credibility purchase and nothing else breaks
B - a hold or a hawkish pause, with the look-through framework winning on a soft core print; GEO-029 should be cut hard if this lands
C - a hike that STEEPENS the curve, the thirty-year pushing past 5.5 per cent as lenders charge more for a policy mix they do not believe in
D - a hike plus a hawkish BoJ producing an eight-per-cent yen move inside 30 days and a levered unwind elsewhere; this is the GEO-025 event

scenarios.falsifier: A soft core CPI followed by a hold means the supply-shock look-through framework governs and this board's 65 per cent on GEO-029 is too hot. A hike into a soft core means the driver is the chair's credibility rather than the data, which is a more durable regime and would justify holding the mark.

scenarios.q: What if the Houthis or Iran hit a Saudi crude EXPORT terminal rather than a refinery?
scenarios.read: Carried forward and now more live, because the attacking side has just acquired coastline and confidence. Everything so far has landed on refining, utilities and an airbase - assets that cost Riyadh money and cost the world diesel. Ras Tanura and Yanbu are a different category: together they load the overwhelming majority of Saudi crude exports, and Ras Tanura alone is the largest offshore loading facility on earth. Hitting one converts a price story into a volume story, and it is the point at which Washington's calculus stops resembling Abqaiq - because Abqaiq was repaired in weeks while a damaged sea-island loading berth is a shipping-schedule problem measured in months. Note the new variable: Pakistan has now publicly said the Mecca defence pact 'will definitely make this agreement operational' if aggression spills further into the kingdom.

stages.s: A - continued strikes on refining, utilities and airbases; Brent holds a war premium in the low hundreds that decays as the shock is absorbed
B - a strike on export infrastructure with loadings interrupted for under a week; Brent takes another leg up on closes
C - sustained export interruption forcing an IEA coordinated release or a US SPR draw
D - a Pakistani or direct US kinetic response against Iranian territory attributed to the terminal strike

scenarios.falsifier: Saudi crude loadings at Ras Tanura and Yanbu holding at recent volumes through 30 September. If they hold while strikes continue, stage A is the correct model and stages C and D should be cut.

Worth logging precisely because the mechanism is now generic: any archive with an anniversary can be re-released into an algorithm that rewards ambiguity.

The checkable kernel is the reorganisation itself; the leap is the motive, and garrison decisions are driven by basing economics, terrain and existing infrastructure far more often than by political geography. Worth watching as a barometer of how seriously Alberta separation is being taken outside Alberta.

chatter.claim: That the holdout juror in the Clancey child-murder trial was got to - threads circulating claims that successive jurors have come forward to condemn a single holdout, framed as evidence of either outside pressure on the panel or a deliberately seeded juror.

chatter.read: The rigged-panel frame, which now attaches to essentially every high-profile acquittal or hung jury. The kernel is unusual in that it is fully public: jurors really are speaking to broadcasters, which is itself the notable fact. What the frame supplies is motive - a holdout with reasons the majority found unpersuasive is the ordinary case, and 'she was got to' is the interpretation that arrives when a verdict feels illegitimate.

chatter.claim: That the sun itself has changed - that it was a warm golden hue within living memory and is now harsh and white and painful to look toward even indirectly, offered as evidence of atmospheric geoengineering, a solar change being concealed, or a switched-out sky.
chatter.spread: A 158-reply /pol/ thread with heavy agreement in replies, recurring across /x/
chatter.read: The changed-sky frame, one of the most persistent and least falsifiable narratives on the boards because the evidence is memory. The checkable kernel is genuinely interesting and mundane: aerosol loading, cataract onset with age, and the near-universal shift from incandescent to LED lighting all plausibly change how bright daylight is perceived. Logged because it is the ambient substrate that geoengineering and chemtrail claims grow out of, and its volume is a decent proxy for how much of the board is in an unfalsifiable register on a given day.

chatter.claim: That entire city districts are props - the fake-cities narrative, in which posters describe small YouTube channels that filmed the entrances of major office buildings from opening to closing hours and recorded almost nobody entering or leaving, offered as evidence that a share of the built environment is a facade maintained for reasons unstated.

Note the lineage the thread claims for itself: it dates its own method to the pizzagate channels, which is a rare case of a narrative correctly identifying its own ancestor.

The distinction the boards are collapsing is the one that matters: a routing and refining constraint is not a geological one, and reading a shipping-lane crisis as depletion is the standard error of this frame. The Cramer provenance of the $150 line is the tell that it is a sentiment reading rather than a supply model.

easy.bottomLine: Diesel - the fuel that moves food, parcels and building materials - passed $6 a gallon in America for the first time ever, which means almost everything gets more expensive over the next few months. In Yemen, the fighters who just took a port town announced that their fighting along the sea passage is finished, but nobody else agreed to that and Saudi Arabia flew 64 air raids in a day. Israel blew up a two-kilometre tunnel system under southern Lebanon with so much explosive that earthquake instruments registered it. And in India, Russia's president landed and China's president is arriving, for a meeting about how countries pay each other without using the American banking system.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, not raised, for the seventh day. This app only moves to its top level if an American is killed or an American ship is hit, and neither happened. The fighters in Yemen said their coastal fighting is over - but saying it does not make it true, and the small island in the middle of the sea passage is still being argued over, not clearly held by anyone. Nothing today crossed the line this app actually watches.
easy.markets: Diesel went past $6 a gallon for the first time in history - the third record in one week, and nearly 60 per cent more expensive than in late February. The reason is not that the world ran out of oil; it is that the factories that turn oil into diesel, and the sea routes that carry it, are both squeezed at once. Crude itself was $107.63 a barrel, high but not a record. Because trucks, tractors and delivery vans all run on diesel, this shows up in food and shipping prices within about one to three months.
brief: The price of diesel in America went above $6 a gallon for the first time ever. That matters more than the price of petrol, because diesel is what trucks, tractors and delivery vans use - so when it goes up, the cost of food and almost everything delivered goes up too, usually a month or three later.

The Houthi fighters who captured the Yemeni port of Mocha announced that their fighting along the coast of the sea passage is now finished. But an announcement by the side that just won ground is not an agreement - nobody else signed it, Saudi Arabia flew 64 air raids in a day, and government forces have moved to the shore right across from the small island that sits in the middle of the passage.

Russia's president Putin landed in India, and China's president Xi is coming too - his first visit to India in almost seven years. The meeting is officially about trade and energy, but the part that really matters is a plan for countries to pay each other in their own currencies instead of going through American banks. India is being careful with its words because America has threatened big taxes on countries that try this.

Israel destroyed a Hezbollah tunnel network more than two kilometres long under a ridge in southern Lebanon. The explosion was so large that earthquake sensors run by the US government recorded it as a 4.1 tremor - which is an independent way of proving how big it was, since nobody in the fight controls those sensors.

Peru agreed to join a US-led group of countries that share intelligence and use their militaries against drug cartels, announced after America's top diplomat visited the capital. It sounds like a police agreement, but it does the work of a military alliance - and unlike a treaty, it did not need any parliament to vote on it. People protested outside over what it means for Peru's independence.

risk.line: HIGH, held for a seventh consecutive pass, and held because the gate this desk publishes did not move. That gate is written in hulls and bodies: a struck US-flagged merchant hull or a confirmed American death. Neither happened. Three things did happen. First, the Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree announced a 'Cessation of Combat Operations along the Coast of Bab al-Mandab Strait' - which is the sound of a side that has finished taking ground declaring the taking finished, and is an announcement rather than an instrument. Note what the wires still will NOT confirm: Reuters-fed copy has government forces relocating to Dhubab, directly on the strait ACROSS from Perim, which means the island in the middle of the door is contested, not held. Second, the price board crossed a threshold that a barrel chart does not show - GasBuddy put the US average diesel price above $6 a gallon for the first time in history, a rise of nearly 60 per cent since late February, with the diesel crack spread at a record $112.17 and US distillate inventories 13 per cent below the five-year average at 106.3 million barrels. Diesel is the price that moves every other price, so this is the oil shock arriving in the part of the economy that cannot substitute. Third, the map widened in two directions the board was not watching: Israel demolished a two-kilometre Hezbollah tunnel system under the Ali al-Taher ridge in Nabatieh with enough explosive to register a 4.1 tremor on the US Geological Survey, and Putin landed in New Delhi where China's foreign ministry confirmed Xi Jinping will join him on 12-13 September - Xi's first visit to India in nearly seven years. Three nuclear-armed heads of state in one room discussing settlement plumbing is not a shooting risk; it is the slower story the shooting is accelerating.

forecasts.q: US diesel crack spread settles back below $45/bbl before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: CUT 3 on a genuinely new variable, and the variable is the ROUTE rather than the barrel or the refinery. This question has been marked down twice already - once on crude-conversion scarcity, once on physical damage to Jazan's conversion capacity. Today's fact is neither: Ansar Allah took Mocha and the Yemeni coast at Bab el-Mandeb, and transits through the strait fell from thirty on Wednesday to twelve on Thursday with a single vessel entering the Red Sea against seventeen the day before. Bab el-Mandeb is the door through which Gulf and Indian diesel reaches Europe; close it and the arbitrage that normally pulls a record crack back toward $45 has to sail around the Cape, adding roughly two weeks and burning the same fuel it is carrying. Hirschman's point about substitutability is the mechanism: a spread mean-reverts when a cheaper source can physically reach the expensive market, and the cheap source just got two weeks further away. Diesel is at a record $5.967 a gallon with the crack at an all-time $108. Capped at 3 because a Cape reroute is expensive, not impossible, and because Atlantic-basin refiners can still supply Europe at a price.

forecasts.q: The FOMC raises the fed funds target range at or before the 9-10 December 2026 meeting
forecasts.note: RAISE 2, deliberately small, and the framework that argues AGAINST it is named and priced rather than mentioned. The ECB raised to 2.5 per cent this morning and said explicitly that it is preparing for LONGER-LASTING inflation - a peer central bank publicly abandoning look-through on the same energy shock, which raises the reputational cost to the FOMC of doing the opposite. US producer prices came in firmer in the details, Brent is $105 to $107, and the horizon here contains THREE meetings, not one, so this is not a bet on Wednesday alone. Against it stands Blinder and Bernanke's finding that central banks have generally and correctly looked THROUGH supply shocks, and the fact that core PPI printed 0.2 against 0.3 expected - the single number still saying this is energy rather than a general inflation. The offset is why this is +2 and not +8. Anchor held at 50: the reference class is a hawkish-chair committee with three standing dissents and three meetings left, and nothing today changes that class.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: CUT 2, and it is the first VOLUME print this question has been given in a fortnight rather than another announcement. Hormuz transits fell to seven on Wednesday against a ten-day average of fourteen; this question needs roughly SIXTY-FIVE a day. The direction of the only admissible evidence class is down, and the level is now four to five per cent of the pre-war baseline rather than the fifty per cent the question asks for. The base rate is the discipline and it is unforgiving: the Suez Canal, closed by a land power holding one bank in June 1967, reopened in June 1975 - eight years - and the Nimbus Moon clearance operation alone took roughly a year AFTER the political agreement to reopen. There is no agreement text here at all. Anchor recomputed 12 to 10, dated today, inputs: seven transits observed 09-09, ten-day average fourteen, baseline about 130. Held to two points because floor effects are real - at four per cent of baseline the remaining downside is small and the question is now almost entirely a bet on whether a political settlement arrives, not on the tape.

forecasts.q: The Algeria-UAE rupture turns material: Algeria names a UAE commercial interest for cancellation or seizure
forecasts.note: OPENED at 40, and it pays a coverage debt this book has named on four separate days without paying: AFRICA has been carried by GEO-023, which is a RUSSIA question that happens to be set in Africa. Resolution: Algeria publicly cancels, suspends, expropriates or refuses to renew a NAMED Emirati commercial interest - port, telecom, energy, logistics or a sovereign-fund stake - before 2027-03-31, per Reuters, AP or AFP. The object exists and is unusually concrete: DP World holds thirty-year concessions over the container terminals at Algiers and Djen-Djen through fifty-fifty joint ventures with the Algerian port authorities, employing more than eight hundred people, with about $108m of committed upgrade capex. BASE RATE first: of the clearest modern ruptures between Arab or Muslim states, three of four produced a material economic instrument within months - Qatar 2017 (blockade), Algeria-Morocco 2021 (the Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline not renewed), Saudi-Canada 2018 (trade and student freeze) - against Turkey-UAE 2018-19, which stayed rhetorical. That is the 40. It is not higher because Algeria's leverage over Abu Dhabi is thin and the terminals are jointly owned, so seizing them damages Algerian throughput first; it is not lower because Algiers has done exactly this before, to Rabat, on a bigger asset.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: CUT 2 after two sessions of deliberate holds, and the dated falsifier published on 09-06 has now RUN. It said the capitals pause would be informative if it lapsed with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text. It lapsed exactly on schedule and Russia put 166 drones, 32 cruise missiles and ballistic and anti-ship rounds into Ukraine within hours, killing five and wounding 63. A truce whose duration matches an envoy's itinerary to the hour is a scheduling accommodation, not a de-escalation - and it demonstrates that Moscow can switch the air campaign on and off at will, which is evidence of confidence rather than exhaustion. Fortna's condition is used a third time and now in the direction that costs us: no monitors, no guarantor, no demarcation, and now a scored falsifier. Only 2 points because Zelenskyy simultaneously said talks are possible this month, and a party that expects to meet is not a party that has walked.

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before Nov expiry
forecasts.note: CUT 2, and the discipline is separating the new fact from the loud one. The loud fact is a record surplus: exports up 25 per cent, the August surplus $119.1bn against $112.5bn in July, $805.5bn year to date, shipments to the US up 34.4 per cent. That is a KNOWN structural condition - China ran $1.2tn last year - and known conditions do not move probabilities. The new fact is that both governments are exploring reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each side, which is the first numbered de-escalation the file has produced since the May truce, sixteen days before a state visit. Composition reinforces it: the surge is in semiconductors, computing hardware and AI-adjacent goods, meaning American demand is pulling the flow. A country importing what it needs is a country that renews.

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly moves toward enrichment or the bomb
forecasts.note: RAISED 2, the smaller of today's two raises, on a demonstrated air-defence shortfall rather than on any nuclear signal. Drones and ballistic missiles reached a coalition airbase at Khamis Mushait and Aramco sites at Abha, Najran and Jazan, wounding 73, on top of direct Iranian strikes on Ras Tanura and Prince Sultan Air Base between February and June. Sagan's security model is the framework: proliferation pressure rises when a state's protector visibly cannot cover it, and Riyadh's revealed strategy through this entire war has been to convert insecurity into a HIGHER PRICE for the American guarantee rather than into an independent programme. That is why this is +2 and not +6 - what today buys is leverage in a guarantee negotiation, and only the failure of that negotiation would buy a programme.

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to US happens in September
forecasts.note: RAISED 1 to the anchor, and a one-point move is all an expected event confirming on schedule is worth. Sixteen days out, with reporting now describing a concrete pre-summit deliverable under negotiation - reciprocal tariff cuts on $30bn of goods each way - rather than only logistics. A summit with a numbered agenda item is marginally harder to cancel than a summit with a guest list.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: HELD, and this is today's most important non-move. Iranian-aligned forces struck four Saudi cities and halted operations at energy facilities; the intuitive read is that an attack on a US ally's oil raises the odds of American strikes on Iran. The base rate says the opposite, and it is the single most relevant analog available: Abqaiq, 14 September 2019, took 5.7 million barrels a day off line - half of Saudi output, the most damaging attack ever on oil infrastructure - was attributed by Washington to Iran directly, and produced NO American strike on Iran. What it produced was a troop deployment and a sanctions round. Damage to Saudi assets has never been the trigger; damage to American ones has. The 09-06 resolution-criteria pin is restated verbatim and still binds: multi-day, state targets inside Iran.

forecasts.q: IF a Hormuz deal happens, it preserves Iranian transit administration
forecasts.note: HELD. Qatar asking for UNCONDITIONAL reopening is, read carefully, evidence on the other side of this question - an unconditional reopening is precisely one that preserves no administrative machinery. But Qatar's ask is not a deal term, and this question resolves on what an agreement CONTAINS, not on what a third party requests. Ostovar's mechanism is unchanged: the Guard converts each crisis into an institution that outlives it.

hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.
