hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: US diesel crosses $6 a gallon for the first time
brief.h: GasBuddy's real-time tracker put the national average diesel price above $6 on Thursday - the third record set in a week, a rise of nearly 60 per cent since late February - with the diesel crack spread at an all-time $112.17 a barrel and US distillate stocks 13 per cent below their five-year average.
brief.t: The important thing here is that this is not a crude story wearing a diesel costume. Brent settled at $107.63 and WTI at $102.48, which are high but not historic; the crack spread - the refiner's margin between a barrel of crude and the diesel made from it - is at an all-time record, and that gap is the whole event. A record crack means the shortage is in the MIDDLE of the barrel, not the top of it: the world has crude and lacks the conversion capacity and the shipping routes to turn it into distillate where distillate is needed. Patrick De Haan of GasBuddy named the transmission in one line - every truck, every delivery, every grocery run just got more expensive - and that is why this print matters more than the Brent print. Gasoline is a consumer complaint; diesel is an industrial input, and it enters the price of food, freight and construction with a lag of roughly one to three months.
brief.context: The mechanism is Hirschman's substitutability point, and it is now failing in three places at once. A crack spread mean-reverts when a cheaper source can physically reach the expensive market - and the cheap sources have all moved further away. US-Israeli strikes took Iranian and Gulf conversion offline; Ukrainian drones on Russian refineries triggered a Russian export ban; China restricted fuel exports; and Bab el-Mandeb, the door through which Gulf and Indian diesel reaches Europe, is now a contested waterway that pushes the arbitrage cargo around the Cape at two extra weeks of sailing, burning the same fuel it carries. Rapidan Energy's Linda Giesecke expects elevated and volatile margins into early 2027, which is the analyst way of saying the reroute is expensive rather than impossible. The base rate worth holding: distillate cracks have spiked to records twice in living memory - 2008 and 2022 - and both times the spike broke within about six months, not because demand fell but because refining runs and routes adjusted. The thing that would break this one is a Red Sea route that clears, and that is not a refining decision.

consp.claim: The circulating claim on the markets boards is that the diesel record is not a supply event at all but the visible edge of terminal depletion - that global oil is genuinely running out, that the Hormuz 'ceasefire' changed traffic by nothing at all and the market is only now catching up, and that $150 crude by year end is already locked in. A parallel thread argues the correct response is to exit every market immediately and hold guns, ammunition, gold, silver and canned food.
consp.spread: Multiple /biz/ threads including a 93-reply all-time-high diesel thread, a 53-reply '$150 is about to be reality' thread built on a viral Cramer post, a 44-reply 'THIS IS NOT A DRILL' exit-everything thread and a 31-reply 'oil is running out' post
consp.read: This is the peak-oil frame reattaching itself to a routing crisis, which is the classic error of reading a transport constraint as a geological one. The checkable kernel is real and boring: distillate inventories genuinely are 13 per cent below the five-year average and the crack genuinely is at a record, so the scarcity is physical - but it is scarcity of conversion and of sea miles, not of hydrocarbons. Note the tell that Cramer is the source of the $150 line; when the retail-facing television voice is the origin, the number is a sentiment reading rather than a supply model.

brief.head: Houthi spokesman declares combat over on the Bab el-Mandeb coast
brief.h: Brigadier General Yahya Saree announced a 'Cessation of Combat Operations along the Coast of Bab al-Mandab Strait' hours after Ansar Allah took the port of Mocha - while Reuters-fed copy still places Yemeni government forces at Dhubab, directly across the water from the island of Perim, and Saudi Arabia flew 64 airstrikes in the preceding 24 hours.
brief.t: Read the announcement as a claim of completion, not a ceasefire - it is what a side says when it has taken what it came for and wants the taking to be treated as settled. That distinction is the whole story, because a cessation announced by the party that just advanced converts a battlefield gain into a status quo without anyone having to agree to it. The load-bearing caveat is geographic and the wires are being careful about it in a way the boards are not: Mocha is a port ON the coast, Perim is the rock IN the door, and government forces relocating TO Dhubab means they are positioning opposite Perim rather than surrendering it. Nobody has published a geolocated image, an admiralty notice or a satellite pass placing Ansar Allah on the island itself. Meanwhile Saudi Arabia is answering with air power at a rate - 64 strikes in a day - that is not the behaviour of a party accepting anyone's declaration of completion.
brief.context: The rail is Mahan's, written in 1890: sea power is not about owning ocean but about owning the narrow places trade must pass. The modern amendment is that a chokepoint does not shut when a ship is hit - it shuts when the Lloyd's Joint War Committee lists it and underwriters stop distinguishing between classes of tonnage, because no owner sails a hull he cannot insure. The deciding desk is therefore an underwriting committee in London, not a command post in Sanaa, and the number to hold is the carve-out: war-risk cover has been pricing Bab el-Mandeb at roughly half a per cent of hull value for general tonnage against as much as three per cent for Saudi-linked ships. That discrimination is the entire reason ships are still sailing. The base rate that should discipline the panic: Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 273 passings a week between 27 July and 23 August, a 15 per cent reduction rather than a closure. What would change the read is a single sentence - a quotation that stops carving Saudi tonnage out - or physical possession of Perim.

angles.effect: GAINS the most valuable thing in the announcement, which is the framing: a self-declared end to operations lets them bank Mocha, Dhubab and the coastline as settled fact while keeping the coercive option, and it costs them nothing because no counterparty signed it.

angles.party: Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council and Tarek Saleh's forces
angles.effect: PAY - a 'cessation' announced by the advancing side after their line collapsed is an invitation to accept the loss, and it arrives while their people are moving south to Lahj and Aden with more than 20,000 displaced in two weeks.

PAYS twice - its Red Sea export corridor at Yanbu now sits behind a coastline it does not control, and it is the only class of tonnage the underwriters are still willing to price separately, which makes its own ships the market's designated target.

angles.party: Shipowners and charterers outside the Saudi carve-out
angles.effect: GAIN, for now - the announcement plus a discriminating war-risk quote is the combination that keeps a 273-a-week route open at a toll rather than closing it, though they carry the risk that the carve-out is a market judgement and not a guarantee.

dec.kill: A war-risk quotation that stops distinguishing Saudi-linked tonnage from general tonnage, or a geolocated image or satellite pass placing Ansar Allah forces on Perim itself. Either one converts this from a completed land grab into a closed strait, and the second is the one the boards keep claiming and the wires keep declining to confirm.

consp.claim: The claim running hardest is that the chokepoint is already gone: that Ansarallah seized the entire coastline overnight and now holds uncontested control of Bab al-Mandab and the Red Sea with the ability to close it at will, that Saudi-backed forces in Yemen have completely collapsed, and that Perim and Zuqar are already taken 'per AFP and Reuters sources'. A separate and louder thread claims the Houthis have just blown up the Saudi East-West pipeline and that the oil market is about to go vertical.
consp.spread: A 251-reply /pol/ thread on total coastal control, a 166-reply 'complete Houthi control' breaking thread, and a 108-reply East-West pipeline thread, alongside the running /pig/ Persia-Israel general
consp.read: The first claim front-runs the evidence in a specific and checkable way - the wires place government forces at Dhubab, across from Perim, which is the opposite of uncontested control, and no imagery has placed Ansar Allah on the island. The pipeline claim has a real kernel and no confirmation: the Petroline runs 1,201km from Abqaiq to Yanbu, Kpler data reported by AFP put Yanbu at roughly 92 per cent of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June, and it HAS been struck this year - in July - so the target is genuine even when tonight's specific claim is unsourced.

brief.head: Putin lands in Delhi as Xi confirms his first India visit since 2019
brief.h: Putin arrived in New Delhi on Thursday for the 18th BRICS summit at Bharat Mandapam on 12-13 September, and China's foreign ministry confirmed Xi Jinping will attend - his first trip to India in nearly seven years - with cross-border payment integration and greater use of national currencies on a published agenda India has been careful to describe as diversification rather than de-dollarisation.
brief.t: The connective move here is to ignore the flags and read the agenda item nobody puts in a photograph: cross-border payment integration and CBDC interoperability. A currency is a headline; a settlement rail is a fact. India has explicitly rejected both a common BRICS currency and an anti-dollar framing - New Delhi's language is local-currency settlement and resilience, which sounds smaller and is actually the more durable ask, because a shared currency requires a shared central bank and a shared rail requires only shared message formats. Follow what each principal is buying. Moscow needs any settlement path that survives sanctions. Beijing prefers a STATE rail - e-CNY and mBridge - over an open one, because an open rail it does not control is just a competitor. Delhi wants the optionality without the tariff bill, which is why the language will stay cautious: Washington has threatened BRICS members with tariffs of up to 100 per cent over exactly this.
brief.context: The rail underneath is the one nobody voted for. Swift already settles roughly three-quarters of cross-border payments inside ten minutes, so the pitch for a replacement is not speed - it is jurisdiction, the ability to move value without a US-reachable chokepoint in the message path. That is why the serious work is happening in plumbing venues rather than summits: the BIS Project Agora real-money tests in July 2026 put cross-border tokenised deposits and central-bank money across seven central banks, which is a netting replacement being trialled rather than talked about. The base rate for summit communiqués is unkind and should be applied here: BRICS declarations have produced working groups, feasibility studies and a development bank, and have not yet produced a rail that clears at scale. What would change the read is a named, dated interoperability pilot with a settlement asset specified - not another paragraph endorsing local-currency trade.

angles.effect: GAINS the room - hosting Xi's first India visit in seven years alongside Putin makes Delhi the venue where the non-Western majority meets, at the precise moment Washington is threatening it with tariffs. He pays by having to keep the language vague enough not to trigger them.

GAINS a legitimacy backdrop and a sanctions-adjacent conversation about settlement, at zero concession - he is attending a summit, not signing a treaty, three days before an FOMC meeting that will price his main export.

GAINS a thaw with a rival he needs neutral and a forum for state-controlled payment infrastructure, but PAYS by legitimising a venue India chairs and by accepting a communiqué watered down for Delhi's tariff exposure.

PAYS in optionality rather than in dollars this week - each interoperability pilot narrows the set of transactions a future sanction can reach, which is a slow erosion of the enforcement franchise rather than a run on the currency.
PAYS in disappointment - the announced object is settlement plumbing, and India has already ruled out the thing the headline promises.

dec.kill: The New Delhi declaration text. If it names a specific rail, a settlement asset and a dated pilot with participating central banks, this is an instrument and the framing verdict is wrong. If it endorses 'greater use of national currencies' and commissions a study, the slogan was the product.

consp.claim: The circulating narrative on the markets and metals boards is that the summit is the visible step in a scheduled transition off the dollar - that governments are openly preparing to seize or freeze private holdings when the switch happens, with Alex Jones cited this week claiming regulators are boasting about plans to confiscate XRP, and that gold, silver and privacy coins are the only assets that survive the changeover.
consp.spread: A 303-reply /pmg/ precious-metals general, a 120-reply XRP schizo general, a 313-reply Monero thread and a 31-reply Alex Jones confiscation thread on /biz/
consp.read: This is the Great Reset frame attaching itself to a genuine and documented institutional programme, which is what makes it sticky. The checkable kernel is real: BIS Project Agora and the CBDC interoperability agenda exist, are official, and are about who can reach a transaction. The unfalsifiable jump is from 'states are building rails they control' to 'states have scheduled a confiscation date' - the first is in published minutes, the second has never had a date that survived its own arrival.

brief.head: Israel blows up a Hezbollah tunnel network in south Lebanon
brief.h: The Israeli military said it demolished a tunnel system running more than two kilometres beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge near Nabatieh, containing a Hezbollah 'Badr' unit command centre plus Iranian-made rockets, missiles, UAVs and hundreds of mines - a detonation large enough to register as a 4.1-magnitude tremor on the US Geological Survey.
brief.t: The seismograph is the story. A demolition that registers 4.1 on an instrument nobody in this conflict controls is an independent measurement of tonnage, and it converts an army's press release into a physical fact - which is exactly why it was done at that scale rather than quietly. This is a message about the terms of the understanding reached after June, not a tactical clearance: Israel is demonstrating that it will treat rebuilt underground infrastructure as inside the envelope of permitted action, and doing it loudly enough that Beirut, Tehran and Washington all read the same number. The distinction that carries the story is announced capability versus destroyed capability. Israel says what was in the tunnel; the tunnel is now unavailable for inspection, so the inventory claim is not checkable and the tremor is.
brief.context: The rail is the ceasefire-that-isn't. A lull followed the June understanding between Iran and the United States and a subsequent Lebanon-Israel arrangement, and strikes have intensified in recent days inside that framework rather than in breach of any published text - which is the durable pattern of this particular kind of arrangement, where the terms are unwritten enough that both parties can operate and neither has to declare it over. Lebanese authorities put the toll from Israeli strikes at more than 4,300 since March. The base rate that matters: post-2006 and post-2024, Hezbollah's tunnel reconstruction has run faster than its rocket reconstitution, because concrete and labour are domestically available and precision guidance is not. That means this demolition buys months of denied position, not a capability reset. What would change the read is a Hezbollah response that is kinetic rather than rhetorical - the group has absorbed a great deal without answering, and the answer, when it comes, is the escalation.

brief.head: Peru joins the US cartel coalition as Rubio ends his Andean tour
brief.h: President Keiko Fujimori announced Peru's membership of the US-led 'Shield of the Americas' - the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, an intelligence-sharing and military-cooperation bloc - after talks in Lima with Marco Rubio, who was awarded the Order of the Sun on the final stop of a three-country, three-day South American tour.
brief.t: The interesting word in the announcement is 'cartel', because it is doing alliance work while wearing a police uniform. A counter-narcotics coalition is politically cheap to join - no one campaigns against fighting cartels - and it delivers the same goods a security treaty would: intelligence sharing, interoperability, a doctrine of greater military involvement in domestic policing, and a standing reason for American personnel and platforms to be present. Follow what each side books. Fujimori gets a hard-security frame for a real domestic problem in extortion and organised crime, and gets it from Washington rather than having to build it. Washington gets the world's second-largest cocaine producer and third-largest copper producer inside a US-led architecture, and gets it without a Senate ratification vote. The Peruvians who pay are the ones who inherit soldiers doing police work, which is the specific transaction the protesters outside were naming when they raised sovereignty and the history of US intervention.
brief.context: The rail is hemispheric: a security architecture is being rebuilt around cartels-as-enemy, and it is filling the space the old ratified treaty structure occupied - with the advantage, from Washington's side, that a coalition can be joined by announcement and cannot be blocked by a legislature. Rubio's three-country tour is the instrument; Peru is the third signature. The base rate is discouraging for the announcement and encouraging for the trend: Latin American security pacts announced at a foreign minister's visit have a poor record of producing standing forces or funded programmes, but a poor record of being unwound either - they accumulate, and the next administration inherits a membership rather than a decision. What would change the read is money and law: a funded programme line, a status-of-forces arrangement, or a Peruvian congressional vote. Absent those, this is a communiqué with a medal attached.

angles.effect: GAINS a hard-security posture and a Washington relationship at the price of a press conference, and imports a doctrine of military involvement in policing that a Peruvian president does not have to legislate for.
GAINS a third Andean signature, a copper-producing partner and a counter-narcotics justification for presence - all through a coalition that requires no treaty ratification and therefore no Senate.

angles.party: Peruvians in the coca and mining regions
angles.effect: PAY - militarised policing lands on the same populations in every prior iteration of this doctrine, and they are not party to an agreement announced at a ministerial visit.

PAY in position - each Andean accession narrows Venezuela's regional room and puts a Chinese copper relationship inside a US-led security frame, which is the actual prize hiding behind the narcotics language.

dec.kill: A funded programme line, a status-of-forces arrangement, or a Peruvian congressional vote. Any of those makes this an instrument rather than an announcement. Twelve months with none of them, and the medal was the deliverable.

watch: Perim, called Mayyun on Arabic charts, and now with a specific observable attached. The wires still place Yemeni government forces at Dhubab ACROSS from the island, so the question is not who claims it but what is on it - Planet Labs imagery documented a roughly 6,150-foot UAE-built runway there in 2025, and an aircraft, radar or air-defence system appearing on that strip would matter far more than any flag on the beach.

Whether Yahya Saree's 'Cessation of Combat Operations along the Coast of Bab al-Mandab Strait' acquires an instrument. An announcement by the advancing side binds nobody. The tests are a notice to mariners, a guarantee any underwriter will actually price, or weekly transit counts recovering toward the 273-a-week Lloyd's List baseline. Saudi Arabia flying 64 airstrikes in the preceding 24 hours is the counter-signal.

The war-risk quotation, and specifically the carve-out that still prices Saudi-linked tonnage separately from everything else. That single distinction is the reason ships are sailing at all. A quote that stops distinguishing classes of tonnage closes the strait more completely than any missile, and it is written by an underwriting committee nobody elected.

US distillate inventories at 106.3 million barrels - 13 per cent below the five-year average - and the diesel crack spread at a record $112.17. This is now the cleanest single read on whether the shock is spreading from energy into general prices, and it lands three days ahead of an FOMC meeting where three members have already dissented for a hike. Rapidan expects elevated, volatile margins into early 2027; that forecast is the thing to score.

The New Delhi declaration text on payments, published 12-13 September. India has already ruled out a common BRICS currency, so the only question that matters is whether the document names a specific rail, a settlement asset and a dated interoperability pilot with participating central banks - or endorses 'greater use of national currencies' and commissions a study. One is an instrument; the other is the slogan being the product.
lesson: Today's lesson is about how a strait actually closes, and it is the difference between watching missiles and watching paperwork. Alfred Thayer Mahan's insight, written in 1890, was that sea power is not about owning ocean but about owning the narrow places where trade must pass - and Bab el-Mandeb, twenty-nine kilometres across, is one of about six such places on earth. But here is the part Mahan could not have known: a modern chokepoint does not shut when a ship is hit. It shuts when the Lloyd's Joint War Committee in London adds it to a listed area and underwriters stop distinguishing between classes of tonnage, because no owner sails a hull he cannot insure and no bank finances a cargo that cannot be covered. Call it closure by quotation. That is why this desk's tripwire is a war-risk quote and not a missile count - a threat that prices at half a per cent of hull value is a toll, and a threat that prices at three per cent is a closure, and the difference is made by an underwriting committee nobody elected. The base rate that should keep you calm and worried at once: the Suez Canal, shut in June 1967 when a land power held one bank, did not reopen until June 1975, and clearing it took roughly a year AFTER the political decision to reopen. Bank-held waterways stay shut for years; missile campaigns are measured in weeks. What that predicts now is testable - watch the weekly Bab el-Mandeb transit counts against the 273-a-week baseline published before Mocha fell, and watch whether one sentence in a war-risk quotation changes. If it does, the strait is closed no matter how quiet the shooting gets.

quiz.q: The brief argues that the Houthi capture of Mocha is more serious than two years of missile attacks on the same waterway. What is the stated mechanism?
options: Mocha is a large oil export terminal, so its loss removes supply from the market
Holding the bank of a 29km strait means shore-launched weapons fired from cover, which cannot be intercepted and can only be reversed by infantry the defending coalition does not have
The Houthis captured advanced anti-ship missiles stored in the port
Mocha gives the Houthis a seat at Yemen's peace negotiations
quiz.why: The distinction is between a threat that can be shot down and a threat that has to be taken back on the ground. Missile campaigns are measured in weeks; the Suez Canal, closed in 1967 when a land power held one bank, took until 1975 to reopen. That asymmetry, not the size of any single attack, is what changed on Thursday.

quiz.q: According to today's lesson, who actually decides whether a strait is 'closed'?
options: The navy with the most ships in the area
The United Nations Security Council, via a formal designation
War-risk underwriters - when a quotation stops distinguishing between classes of tonnage, owners stop sailing and banks stop financing cargo
The country that owns the nearest coastline
quiz.why: Call it closure by quotation. No owner sails a hull he cannot insure and no bank finances an uncoverable cargo, so the operative decision sits with the Lloyd's Joint War Committee and the P&I clubs rather than with any navy. That is why this desk's tripwire is a premium, not a missile count.

quiz.q: This board removed its Brent band question from the open list today because Brent closed at $101.21, resolving it NO. What does the brief say the good score should actually be credited to?
options: Correctly predicting that the Houthis would seize Mocha
A barrier recalculation - specifically a discrete-monitoring correction worth fourteen points of survival probability, applied because the question resolves on daily closes
Following the consensus of oil analysts
Cutting the probability at the last possible moment
quiz.why: The mark went from 65 per cent to 17 in sixteen days almost entirely through geometry rather than opinion: the distance to the barrier, the realised volatility, and a continuity correction required because the question resolves on closes rather than intraday prints. A method that can be re-run is worth more than a call that happened to land.

quiz.q: Two branches of the US government were pulling in opposite directions today. What was the collision, and where is it being priced?
options: Congress and the White House disagreed on Yemen policy; it is priced in defence stocks
Fiscal loosening - a promised $5,000-per-adult payment worth over $1tn - against monetary tightening into an oil shock, priced in the thirty-year Treasury yield at 5.36 per cent
The Supreme Court and the president disagreed on redistricting; it is priced in polling
The Fed and the ECB disagreed on inflation; it is priced in the euro
quiz.why: This is Putnam's two-level game: a leader plays the domestic board and the foreign board at once, and the moves that win one can lose the other. Here the domestic board is a five-seat House majority and the foreign board is the auction desk that has to roll roughly $9tn of debt. The long end is where the two meet and where the disagreement acquires a price.

quiz.q: A claim is circulating that the $5,000 payment promise proves the administration privately knows an economic break is coming. Which observable would best settle whether the promise is policy or a turnout instrument?
options: Whether the president repeats the promise at more rallies
Whether the stock market rises or falls over the next month
Whether introduced bill text appears with a named sponsor and a CBO score before November
Whether polling for the president's party improves
quiz.why: The caveat that carries this story is announcement versus instrument. Two promises of exactly this shape were made earlier this cycle - the DOGE savings dividend and the $2,000 tariff cheque - and neither was ever paid. Note also the logical move the claim makes: it infers private knowledge from a public incentive, when an eight-week-out midterm with a five-seat margin already explains the behaviour completely.

sections.t: US diesel set an all-time record this week at $5.820 a gallon, and the crack spread — the refiner's fee for turning crude into something an engine can burn — printed an all-time $108 a barrel while Brent sat at an unremarkable $96. In the same week US missiles reportedly struck a tanker at Iran's Kharg Island anchorage, and Ukrainian drones held Russian refinery runs at 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since May 2002.

Crude — the thing everyone photographs and embargoes — is behaving; refined product is not. A $108 crack means the market will pay more to convert a barrel than the barrel is worth: a fact about cokers and hydrotreaters, not about oil. Name the mechanism — the conversion bottleneck. The binding constraint is never the abundant input but the narrow step in the middle, which cannot be built on the timescale of a war or an election.

sections.h: Deep history I — Rockefeller never wanted the oil
sections.t: John D. Rockefeller owned almost no wells. He owned the refineries of Cleveland, and what he did with them in 1871 is the founding text of chokepoint economics. Tom Scott of the Pennsylvania Railroad chartered the South Improvement Company, and Rockefeller's terms inside it were breathtaking: the Erie, New York Central and Pennsylvania would pay the SIC a rebate of $1.06 on every barrel it shipped — and a drawback of $1.06 on every barrel shipped by refiners outside the club. He was paid when his rivals did business. The charter was repealed that April before a single transaction cleared, and Ida Tarbell's exposé later finished the job — but the insight outlived the scandal: crude is worthless until someone converts and moves it, and whoever owns the narrow step prices the wide one.

sections.h: Deep history II — the war decided at the still
sections.t: The largest test of this proposition was the Allied air war, fought inside the alliance before it was fought over Germany. Arthur Harris of RAF Bomber Command believed in punishment: burn the cities, break the will. Carl Spaatz and Arthur Tedder pushed what Harris dismissed as panacea targets — oil. Germany had almost no crude. It had Bergius hydrogenation, synthetic fuel pressed from coal at Leuna, Pölitz and Brüx, plants too enormous to hide. The oil plan began in May 1944. Leuna alone absorbed 22 raids, 6,552 bomber sorties and 18,328 tons of bombs across a year, behind Europe's heaviest flak concentration. It worked anyway. German synthetic output fell from a peak of 316,000 tons a month to 107,000 in June 1944 and 17,000 by September. Aviation gasoline — the specific fraction, not oil in general — went from 175,000 tons in April to 5,000 in September: 97% gone in five months. From May 1944 Germany consumed more than it produced every month, and the stockpile was gone in six.

sections.h: Deep history II — the fuel, not the factories
sections.t: The detail that makes it unforgettable: over the same period Albert Speer drove German tank and aircraft PRODUCTION to its wartime peak. The Reich ended 1944 with more airframes than it could fly and more panzers than it could move — the factories were fine and the fuel was not. The US Strategic Bombing Survey — written by people with every reason to praise bombing in general — judged the oil and transport campaigns decisive and the city campaign not. Japan lost the same way: the July 1941 freeze is remembered as an oil embargo, but the fatal shortage was 100-octane aviation gasoline, a conversion capability Japan could not build.

sections.h: Deep history III — how the West stopped building stills
sections.t: Now the slow part. The last greenfield major refinery built in the United States was Marathon's Garyville, Louisiana: built 1973-76, online 1977, still running at 596,000 barrels a day. Fifty years, no new plants — and the base is now shrinking: about 132 operable refineries in January 2025 against more than 300 in 1981, with roughly 1.235m b/d of distillation capacity removed in seven recent closures and conversions, over 6.5% of the total. All of it while shale made America the largest crude producer in history at 13.86m b/d. The country built the well and stopped building the still. The capacity emigrated rather than vanished — Jamnagar runs 1.24m b/d, Dangote opened at 650,000 and plans 1.4m, China kept building — so the toll moved east and south, to jurisdictions happy to buy discounted sanctioned crude and sell the product back to the people imposing the sanctions.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: In all three cases the scarce thing is the transformation, and transformation capacity is inelastic over any politically relevant horizon: a new crude supplier takes a fortnight, a new hydrocracker takes five years and a billion dollars. Ukraine is now running the 1944 oil plan at a ten-thousandth of the cost, a drone flying 1,550km to Omsk doing what 6,552 B-17 sorties did to Leuna — Pape's denial thesis tested live. It breaks against me here: Germany had no crude and no neutral supplier, Russia has both, and a 24-year low in refining has not stopped Pokrovsk.

sections.h: The adjudication — Yergin and Blas vs Chris Miller
sections.t: THE ADJUDICATION — YERGIN AND BLAS versus CHRIS MILLER Yergin and Blas hold that energy chokepoints self-heal — inventories, bypass and rerouting absorb shocks forecast to be fatal — and they have been right about the barrel, Brent at $96 in a war that curtailed over 11m b/d. Chris Miller's Chip War argues the opposite for inputs that are not fungible: no reserve of fabs, no bypass for EUV, a decade to rebuild. The evidence splits them by step. Yergin and Blas won the crude argument; the crack is the market announcing the win does not survive one step downstream, because there is no strategic reserve of cokers — the US holds hundreds of millions of barrels of crude in the SPR and about a million barrels of distillate in the Northeast reserve, having stockpiled the input it cannot burn. Miller's case is still weaker in oil than in silicon: diesel is shippable in a way a fab's output is not, so refining heals in 12-24 months rather than 12-24 days.

OECD gasoline demand is in structural decline as EVs scale; diesel and jet demand are not, because trucks, ships, aircraft, mining and data-centre backup have no substitute. But a refinery makes every cut at once, so the economics that close Western refineries — falling gasoline — destroy the distillate capacity nobody meant to lose. A trap, not a cycle; confidence high. The bolder call, near 60%: by the mid-2030s the US is at once the world's largest crude exporter and a chronic net importer of middle distillates, and that buys a strategic PRODUCT reserve — legislated storage of diesel and jet, enacted after a winter shortage rather than before one. What keeps this honest is GEO-026: does the US diesel crack settle below $45 before 15 December 2026? It sits at 35%, so the house is 65% on regime rather than outage — and if the crack mean-reverts on the 2022 schedule, this is an elegant story about a spike, published as a miss.
